title: Changelog output formats and their mode rules
expectation: Changelog outputs are validated, not just parsed. A `json` (or `text`) output without `mode = "release"` is a configuration error that names the output and the rule, because those formats describe a single release rather than a cumulative file. With the mode set, the output renders machine-readable notes that carry the change summary. `append` mode is the opposite contract: it accumulates, so two successive releases leave two headings in the same changelog file rather than the second overwriting the first.

checks.command:
cp monochange.toml .cfg.bak; printf '
[changelog.outputs.jsonreport]
stream = "user"
targets = ["main"]
path = "release-notes/{{ version }}.json"
format = "json"
' >> monochange.toml; monochange step validate > .cf.out 2>&1; rc=$?; grep -q 'must use `mode = "release"` with format `json`' .cf.out; a=$?; mv .cfg.bak monochange.toml; rm -f .cf.out; test $rc -eq 1 -a $a -eq 0
checks.why: The mode rule is enforced at config load, not at render time, so a CI artifact config that forgets it must be rejected before it can produce a silently wrong file.

checks.command:
cp monochange.toml .cfg.bak; printf '
[changelog.outputs.jsonreport]
stream = "user"
targets = ["main"]
path = "release-notes/{{ version }}.json"
format = "json"
mode = "release"
' >> monochange.toml; mkdir -p .changeset; printf -- '---
"@acme/ui": feature
---

Copy link button on the profile screen
' > .changeset/u.md; monochange notes --output jsonreport 2>/dev/null > .jr.out; rc=$?; python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(open('.jr.out')); assert 'summary' in d and 'title' in d, sorted(d)"; j=$?; rm -f .jr.out .changeset/u.md; mv .cfg.bak monochange.toml; test $rc -eq 0 -a $j -eq 0
checks.why: With the mode satisfied the same output must render parseable JSON carrying the release summary, which is what downstream automation consumes.

checks.command:
git init -b main -q && git add -A && git -c user.name=A -c user.email=a@a.dev commit -qm init >/dev/null 2>&1; mkdir -p .changeset; printf -- '---
"@acme/api": patch
---

Honor the caller abort signal
' > .changeset/a.md; monochange prepare >/dev/null 2>&1; printf -- '---
"@acme/api": fix
---

Guard against an empty body
' > .changeset/b.md; monochange prepare >/dev/null 2>&1; grep -c '^## ' packages/api/CHANGELOG.md | grep -qx '2'
checks.why: The default `append` mode inserts each release at the top of the existing file. Overwriting instead of accumulating would silently destroy release history, which is the regression this pins. Runs last because it mutates the tree.
